facts.statement: Chuanjiesaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs that lived during the Middle Jurassic Period.
facts.quote: Chuanjiesaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs from the middle Jurassic Period.

facts.statement: Chuanjiesaurus lived in what is now China.
facts.quote: They lived in what is now China.

facts.statement: Fossils of Chuanjiesaurus were found in the Chuanjie Formation near the village of Chuanjie in Yunnan Province, China, and the genus is named after this location.
facts.quote: Fossils of the species were found in the village of Chuanjie, Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, (in Chuanjie Formation deposits) and are named after the location where the fossils were discovered.

facts.statement: Holtz estimated the length of Chuanjiesaurus to be 25 meters (82 feet).
facts.quote: Holtz gave a length of 25 meters (82 ft).

facts.statement: Chuanjiesaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
Chuanjiesaurus was initially considered a cetiosaurid but is now classified as a mamenchisaurid.
facts.quote: Inicialmente considerado un cetiosáurido, actualmente se le considera un mamenquisáurido.

facts.statement: Chuanjiesaurus lived approximately 168 million years ago during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 168 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Chuanjiesaurus was longer than other eusauropods of its time, reaching 25 meters in length with a very long neck.
facts.quote: Era más largo que otros eusaurópodos de la época, llegando a los 25 metros de largo y poseía un cuello muy largo.

facts.statement: The species is known from 20 articulated vertebrae (9 from the neck), scapula, humerus, other limb bones, and rib fragments from at least three individuals.
facts.quote: Conocido por 20 vértebras articuladas, 9 de ellas del cuello, escápula, húmero, otros huesos de los miembros y fragmentos de costillas de al menos 3 individuos.

facts.statement: The time range for Chuanjiesaurus is estimated between 170.9 and 168.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The type species Chuanjiesaurus anaensis was first described by Fang, Pang, Lü, Zhang, Pan, Wang, Li, and Cheng in 2000.
rejected.quote: The type species, Chuanjiesaurus anaensis, was first described by Fang, Pang, Lü, Zhang, Pan, Wang, Li and Cheng in 2000.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'The type species Chuanjiesaurus anaensis was first described'
